sections.text: But those who act righteously, in whom sin has been destroyed, who are free from the infatuation of the conflicting emotions, they worship Me with firm resolution.
Those who make Me their refuge, who strive for liberation from decay and Death, they realise the Supreme Spirit, which is their own real Self, and in which all action finds its consummation.
साधिभूताधिदैवं मां साधियज्ञं च ये विदुः।
Those who see Me in the life of the world, in the universal sacrifice, and as pure Divinity, keeping their minds steady, they live in Me, even in the crucial hour of death.

Just to remind us: the Bhagavad Gita is divided into three segments of six chapters each. In the first segment, we learned all about ourselves. The second chapter gave us a summary of who we are.
What we remember from the second chapter is that the self is immutable, imperishable. The myself which I consider me is immutable, imperishable. But we never fully grasped what that really means. Okay, someone who realizes that -- how would he act? How would he behave in this world? Will he be completely different from us?
We saw the characteristics of a Gnani, but that didnt show us anything different from what we do. So the next few chapters gave us how to analyze our actions and ourselves, and then recalibrate our actions to become more productive and effective. That first segment ended with Chapter 6 on meditation. Meditation is the means given to us to recalibrate this instrument called mind, body, and intellect.
Then this next segment of six chapters, from 7 to 12, is all about what that imperishable self is which we talked about in Chapter 2. Thats why the first chapter of this segment, Chapter 7 -- Gnana Vignana Yoga -- is about having this knowledge of the Lord, that immutable self we learned about in Chapter 2.
But how can we make it Vishishta Gnana that we can apply? Therefore Chapter 7 describes in detail the Lords nature and why we cant realize it in our day-to-day life. Bhagavan said, I manifest in this world as the Eightfold Prakriti. Thats something you and I can see -- thats nothing but my own manifestation. Then he says, There is nothing in this world which does not come out of me. Anything you can see, feel, touch, and perceive has come out of me and will dissolve in me.
And all this world of plurality, as we see it, is strung together. Nothing is independent, like an island in this universe -- which is hinting at us, because we think we are the island of the universe as me and everything else revolves around me. He said, No, everything is strung like pearls in a necklace. I am that common thread. I pervade through this universe as the Eightfold Prakriti.
You are part of that Prakriti. The unmanifest is the common thread among all the manifestations which apparently look different from each other. Why then are we not seeing that? Because you are under the spell of my divine Maya, which creates plurality out of singularity. As long as you are under that spell, you see yourself as different from this world. This Maya has three Gunas -- Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas -- and through their permutation and combination, it creates the infinite varieties of things and beings.
But as long as I cant overcome that Maya, I cant see the truth. In the last set of verses we saw: Iccha dvesha samutthena dvandva mohena Bharata. Because of this desire or that desire, I have divided this world into two -- the world I like and the world I dont like. Right from birth, Im deluded about myself.
That immutable, imperishable self talked about in Chapter 2 -- Im not recognizing it because of the duality my mind has created. My mind says, This is me and everything else is the world. As long as I cant get out of that concept, Bhagavan said, I wont be able to realize the truth.
However, in the last three verses he says that those Gnanis who have erased this wrong notion of who they are -- their papas are all erased by this new line of thinking. Yesham tu antagatam papam jananam punya karmanam.
So there is hope. Bhagavan said this is not just a philosophical discussion. Hes not just telling us, You will never realize it. No, lets figure out what the problem was in the beginning. The problem was my wrong line of thinking: that I am different from this world. This notion that I am this limited being, and therefore I have all these problems.
Once I undo the thinking that I am this limited being, the limitation will be gone. Yesham tu antagatam papam -- those whose papas have come to an end. The classic definition of Papa is: a thought or impression which takes me away from myself, takes me away from my understanding that I am that immutable, imperishable self, and creates division between I and the world. As long as I am driven by the desires of the flesh, my thinking will be focused on how to fulfill those desires.
When I start thinking in the same line, it creates deep channels in my mind which guide subsequent thoughts into the same channel. This habit of following the same line of thinking to fulfill desires creates Papa -- because I just cant get out of the thinking that this will make me happy. Last time I had a cup of coffee and it made me happy. This time it should do the same thing, and I continue. Bhagavan said, that creates your own notion of who you are.
How do I come out of it? He said, more and more I become introverted through the technique given in the previous chapter -- the meditation that No, this is not me. The one who is getting happy with the Starbucks coffee is not me; it is someone other than myself. That line of thinking erases those channels created by my attempt to satisfy all the desires that body, mind, and intellect have created. The more I fulfill desires, the more new experiences create new channels of thinking, which create new Vasanas.
These Vasanas, the tendencies, create the same line of thinking and the same line of actions. I need to stop doing actions driven by the same line of thinking that is not giving me happiness. Even though I figured out last time that investing in the stock market was not good -- because everybody says, Dont miss this cycle, Im back again. You need to get out of that line of thinking.
Once you start meditating on what really makes you happy -- if I analyze my experience, was it the experience that made me happy, or something else? -- you come to the conclusion that no desire makes me happy. When Im completely at ease, when I dont want anything -- Ive already eaten my lunch, I dont have anywhere to go, and I can just sit down -- at least I still have a desire to watch TV, but even if I drop that, Ill probably be completely happy.
This new line of thinking creates the undoing of all those wrong channels in my mind. Now I have removed all the Papas. Papas are just the wrong line of thinking, the wrong Vasanas.
Yesham tu antagatam papam jananam punya karmanam. The method we learned in the first six chapters is Karma Yoga -- selfless actions. When I act in a manner that erases the thinking that working to fulfill my desires makes me happy, I also realize the real happiness comes when I do something for others -- the true happiness we get when we do something for our children, our parents, our relatives, our friends.
Jananam punya karmanam -- they have changed their line of actions, therefore changed their line of thinking, therefore changed their tendencies. Now they are in a completely different realm of actions and thinking. Their Papas are all erased.
Te dvandva moha nirmuktah -- now they are out of this duality. Im not just working for me; Im working for the whole of humanity, my town, my family. I keep expanding my identity until there is no duality between I and the world. Te dvandva moha nirmuktah -- this Dvandva is nothing but a delusion that you and I are different from each other.
That this world and I are two different entities is nothing but a delusion. Those who, by acting in the right manner, erase those lines of thinking which create delusion -- now Bhajante mam dridha vratah. Worshipping, we have seen, is an act of love. That love for the divine becomes so firm that I am firmly established in the thought that I and the world are nothing but part of the same all-pervading entity.
The next verse says Jara marana mokshaya -- and why am I doing all of this? Because the two things Im afraid of in life are Jara (old age) and Marana (death). We had a Valentines Day party yesterday, and you know what the topic was -- because we were all probably above 50 there.
How do we get out of this problem of dying? The 10 tubes going through you... Because we are afraid of Jara, old age -- when I will not be in control. I was reading about Ronald Reagan, when he was taking a walk and people said, Good morning, Mr. President. He wouldnt recognize why people were calling him president. He didnt know he was a president. He just thought, This guy is nice; hes greeting me.
Thats all he could think. The thought that a person can reach that level, where he cant even recognize who he is -- its pretty scary for all of us. Because all our life we took pride in being in control. I take care of myself. I take care of my family. I take care of my business.
I take care of... -- I am in charge is what makes me who I am. The very thought that I will not be in control is very, very disturbing. We want to get out of that. I want to exist, and death wipes me out. It just doesnt seem right.
Jara Marana Mokshaya -- for liberation from this thought of old age and death. Mam ashritya -- taking complete refuge in me means not Lord Krishna or Rama or Jesus, but in that immutable self. Taking complete refuge in identification with my immutable self. Just as Im in complete control in a barbers chair -- the hair I let go and the hair I keep, Im in complete control. The hair I let go, I dont get attached to.
Please, please pack it up for me! No -- I say, Wipe it out clean as quickly as possible.

Those who act righteously, in whom sin has been destroyed, who are free from the infatuation of conflicting emotions, they worship Me with firm resolution. Sin (papa) here is defined not as breaking commandments but as any thought or action that reinforces the illusion of separation between self and the Divine. Each time you act from ego, from the belief that you are a separate, isolated being fighting against the world, you deepen those grooves of wrong thinking. Each time you act from dharma, recognizing your connection to the whole, those grooves begin to fill in. Today, before each significant action, ask: Does this reinforce my sense of separation, or does it align me with something greater?
The chapter concludes with the profound motivation for spiritual seeking: liberation from decay and death (jara-marana-mokshaya). This is not morbid but urgently practical. We all fear aging and death because our identity is bound to the body. The one who knows the Self as distinct from the body has nothing to fear, like someone in a barbers chair watching hair fall away without grief. Today, contemplate: What in you is actually subject to decay? Your body certainly. Your opinions and preferences, yes. Your memories and personality, these too change. But the awareness that witnesses all these changes, has that ever aged?
The final verses point to the culmination: knowing the Divine in all aspects of existence, as Adhibhuta (in all beings), Adhidaiva (as the cosmic principle), and Adhiyajna (as the sacred offering in every action). The promise is extraordinary: Those who know Me thus, even at the hour of death, remain united with Me. Today, practice the recognition that every action, however mundane, can be a sacred offering. Washing dishes, answering emails, driving to work, when done with awareness of the Divine presence pervading all, these become Yajna, sacrifice, paths to liberation.
